name: Context-Switch with Stash
problem: You are halfway through a feature when an urgent bug report comes in. You need to switch branches to fix the bug, but your current changes are messy and aren't ready to be committed.

steps.title: Stash your uncommitted work
steps.description: Temporarily shelve your current changes. Adding a message helps you remember what this stash was for.
steps.code:
git stash push -m "WIP: new checkout flow"

# Your working directory is now clean.

steps.title: Switch branches and fix the bug
steps.description: Now that your directory is clean, you can safely switch to the main branch to address the urgent issue.
steps.code:
git checkout main
git checkout -b hotfix-checkout-bug
# ... fix bug, commit, push ...

git checkout main
git merge hotfix-checkout-bug

steps.title: Return to your feature and restore work
steps.description: Go back to where you left off and pop the stash to re-apply your unfinished changes.
steps.code:
git checkout feature-checkout
git stash pop

# Your messy changes are back exactly as you left them!

alternatives.title: Commit as WIP instead
alternatives.description: Some developers prefer making a 'WIP' commit instead of stashing, because commits are harder to lose than stashes.
alternatives.code:
git commit -am "WIP: do not push"
# ... switch branches, fix bug, come back ...
git reset HEAD~1  # Undo the WIP commit but keep changes
